function: Learned joint control of inner-beam beamwidth and per-beam transmit power (strict FFR) in a multi-beam LEO satellite downlink to minimize normalized capacity deviation (pp. 7-9).
system: LEO satellite, 600 km, 512-element circular phased array, 6 deg outer and 3-5 deg inner beams, single-antenna terminals, 40 GHz Q-band, no RIS (pp. 5, 10-11).
method: Reinforcement learning: cooperative multi-agent, value-based CTDE (QTRAN loss) with per-beam Q-networks and a joint Q-network, two hidden layers of 64 neurons, replay buffer (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom LoS model with free-space loss and antenna patterns, no small-scale fading (p. 7); vessel positions from real AIS data, random per-user demands 5-35 Mbps (p. 11).
test_conditions: Trained 220 episodes x 24 steps (p. 11); inference evaluated on 24 test samples (Fig. 10, p. 13); paper does not describe unseen scenarios, bands or beam counts.
baselines: Non-learned: genetic algorithm (near-optimal benchmark), fixed beamwidth (two values), full frequency reuse, random actions. Learned: independent DQL (I-DQL); single-agent DQL only analysed for complexity (pp. 13-14).
metrics: Normalized capacity deviation (NCD) relative to GA, averaged as 84% for CTDE versus 60% for I-DQL; episode reward, per-agent fairness, action entropy, control-loop latency (pp. 5, 11-14).
complexity: Big-O training and inference complexity per method (Eq. 32, Table 5, p. 14); CTDE inference O(Cenv(U)+B*Pc), linear in beams; training about 25 minutes on CPU (p. 11).
openness: Dataset openly accessible at https://cloud.cttc.es/index.php/s/5YbGTTstnxypabQ (p. 15); no code release stated.
q1_support: p. 7: "while small-scale fading is neglected". The channel is a custom clear-sky LoS model (free-space loss, antenna gains); no 3GPP TR 38.811/38.901, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model is named. AIS data (p. 11) give vessel positions only, not measured channels.
q2_support: p. 13: "the performance comparison is performed against multiple benchmarks to evaluate its inference capabilities". No unseen scenario, band, number of beams or adaptation is reported; only one environment (Table 3, p. 10) is described.
q3_support: p. 13: "a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed" and "I-DQL represents a non-cooperative multi-agent scheme"; p. 14, Fig. 11: normalized NCD of CTDE vs GA, I-DQL, fixed beamwidth, full FR and random. I-DQL is independent DQL, counted as the standard learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 14: "the overall training complexity can be expressed as" O(E x T x (Cenv(U) + 2(BPc + Pjoint))); Table 5 lists training and inference complexity per method; p. 11: "requires approximately 25 minutes".
q5_support: p. 15: "The dataset is openly accessible through the following link" https://cloud.cttc.es/index.php/s/5YbGTTstnxypabQ. No code release is stated.
notes: Include, area 6: learned control of beamwidth and transmit power of satellite beams is physical-layer NTN beam and power control; the frequency plan (inner FR 1, outer FR 4) and scheduling are fixed or exogenous (pp. 5-6). Tables 3-5 and Figs. 10-11 were read from page images. q1 borderline: AIS data are real vessel positions, not channel measurements, and the channel is a custom LoS model (p. 7), so 0; reviewer may confirm. q3 borderline: I-DQL (independent DQN agents, no joint critic) is counted as a standard learned baseline on the same problem; if the reviewer treats it as an ablation of the CTDE method, q3 becomes 0. Single-agent DQL is not simulated, only analysed for complexity (p. 14). q2: no test on unseen conditions.
